question_record.context: A recent incident involved using PsExec to remotely execute commands, potentially indicating lateral movement attempts by an attacker. Specifically, the commands executed include `notepad.exe` and `cmd.exe`, with `cmd.exe` having a Process ID of 8656 and timestamp `2024-06-20t09:07:09.5458894z`. This activity suggests attackers may be targeting devices within the organization.
question_record.question: In relation to this sequence of activities, there was also a possible attempt to access the Primary Refresh Token (PRT). Can you identify the file name of the process used in this attempt?
solution: PsExec launched a command on a remote device with AadDeviceId `4d8d23e9-a77d-4e33-9435-b8c457e57ca1`.
There was a possible attempt to access the Primary Refresh Token using the process `powershell.exe`.

84.name: PsExec launched a command on a remote device
84.description: PsExec was used to launch a command on a remote device. PsExec is a tool used to launch programs on remote, or local devices. An attacker might be leveraging this tool to launch malicious commands to a remote device and move laterally in the organization.

36.name: Possible attempt to access Primary Refresh Token (PRT)
36.description:
Possible attempt to access Primary Refresh Token (PRT) has been detected. A Primary Refresh Token (PRT) is a key artifact of Azure AD authentication on Windows 10, Windows Server 2016 and later versions, iOS, and Android devices. It is a JSON Web Token (JWT) that's specially issued to Microsoft first party token brokers to enable single sign-on (SSO) across the applications used on those devices. Attackers can attempt to access this resource to move laterally into organization or perform credential theft.

For more information, read the Activity profile: Midnight Blizzard credential attacks Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/e4aad043-a273-4f88-b65e-fdfc3996ec92/analystreport?

steps.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT o.AlertId, o.AlertTitle, o.ObservedAt, o.EntityIndex,
       o.GraphValue AS value, o.RawComponents, o.Roles, o.SourceRowHash,
       i.GraphValue AS matched_input
FROM LTMInputEvidence i
JOIN LTMEntityEvidence o ON o.SourceRowHash = i.SourceRowHash
WHERE i.AlertTitle = %s
  AND i.Concept = 'Command_File_Mention' AND o.Concept = 'Device_AAD_ID'
  AND i.GraphValue IN (%s,%s)
ORDER BY o.AlertId, o.SourceRowHash, o.EntityIndex, o.GraphValue, i.GraphValue
LIMIT 501
parameters: PsExec launched a command on a remote device
